label: MHA overall rank
definition: Overall ranking across all 17 MHA measures (adult and youth, prevalence and access). States with positive outcomes are ranked higher (closer to one) than states with poorer outcomes (closer to 51). The overall, adult, youth, prevalence, and access rankings were analyzed by calculating a standardized score (Z score) for each measure and ranking the sum of the standardized scores. The majority of measures represent data collected up to 2023. An overall ranking of 1-13 indicates lower prevalence of mental illness and higher rates of access to care; 39-51 indicates higher prevalence and lower rates of access. The combined scores of all 17 measures make up the overall ranking.
source_title: The State of Mental Health in America 2025
vintage: 2025 edition; "the majority of measures represent data collected up to 2023"
suppressed_note: No suppressed values in these tables. Rank tables have no national row, so the US cell is empty for ranks.
caveats: 2025 is the current edition on mhanational.org as of 2026-10-03; no 2026 edition was posted. 51 ranked jurisdictions (50 states + DC). The US row for measure values is MHA's "National" row.

The overall, adult, youth, prevalence, and access rankings were analyzed by calculating a standardized score (Z score) for each measure and ranking the sum of the standardized scores. The majority of measures represent data collected up to 2023. An overall ranking of 1-13 indicates lower prevalence of mental illness and higher rates of access to care; 39-51 indicates higher prevalence and lower rates of access. The combined scores of all 17 measures make up the overall ranking.
source_title: The State of Mental Health in America 2025
vintage: 2025 edition; "the majority of measures represent data collected up to 2023"
suppressed_note: No suppressed values in these tables. Rank tables have no national row, so the US cell is empty for ranks.
caveats: 2025 is the current edition on mhanational.org as of 2026-10-03; no 2026 edition was posted. 51 ranked jurisdictions (50 states + DC). The US row for measure values is MHA's "National" row.

label: CCBHC status of state (SAMHSA map)
definition: Category assigned to the state in the description of SAMHSA's 2026 map of CCBHCs: participating in the Section 223 CCBHC Medicaid Demonstration; approved to launch a Demonstration program starting July 1, 2026; CMS-approved payment method for CCBHCs via state plan amendment or 1115 waiver separate from the Demonstration; at least one local SAMHSA expansion grantee; or no CCBHCs.
source_title: Section 223 Medicaid CCBHC Demonstration and State Programs
vintage: Map "ccbhc-map-2026"; page last updated 07/06/2026
suppressed_note: US cell empty.
caveats: The state lists come from the alt text of SAMHSA's map image, which assigns each state to exactly one category, while the map legend categories can overlap. The page text says eight states joined the Demonstration in 2017 (naming only Pennsylvania, which withdrew in 2019, and Nevada, which moved its program out in 2023); the page does not name the other six, and the alt text's 12-state 'participating in CCBHC Medicaid Demonstration' list may therefore omit earlier-cohort states that the alt text files under 'CMS-approved payment method'. Treat the 'demonstration' list as what SAMHSA's alt text states, not as a verified complete roster.
